name: Motor-Driven Cycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle and no more than three wheels whose electric motor puts out less than 1,000 watts (or whose engine is over 35 cc and under 150 cc). An electric two-wheeler past the moped limits but under 1,000 watts lands here.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle for each rider, and no more than three wheels on the ground
An electric motor with a power output of less than 1,000 watts, or a combustion engine over 35 cc and under 150 cc
One that also stays within 2 brake horsepower, 750 watts and 35 mph is a moped
May never be ridden faster than 35 mph, or faster than the posted limit
Riders need a Class A, B, C or D license with a motorcycle endorsement; riders 17 and younger must complete a state-approved basic rider course

From 14, after a basic rider course, a restricted Class D license with a motorcycle-only restriction allows riding only 4:30 a.m. to 9 p.m., in a helmet, and accompanied by a licensed rider 21 or older in visual contact until the rider passes the driving test
May be barred from a controlled-access roadway where signs are posted
Riders under 16 may not carry passengers; older riders may carry one only on a factory double seat with footrests and wheels at least 12 inches in diameter
May not pass other vehicles between lanes of traffic
